crater.label: Impact crater
crater.description: Bowl-shaped impact structures. Uses the radial profile and depth/diameter.

base_highland.label: Base site: ridge / plateau
base_highland.description: Elevated, fairly flat ground with long sunlight at a low sun, like the Artemis south-pole regions.

periglacial_plains.label: Ice-rich plains
periglacial_plains.description: Low, smooth plains with ground ice and periglacial landforms, like proposed Mars landing sites.

dunes.label: Dune field
dunes.description: Wind-built sand dunes. Needs high-resolution DEMs (HiRISE/CTX) on the Mars side.

volcanic.label: Volcanic terrain
volcanic.description: Lava flows, cones, tuyas and lava tubes.

evaporite.label: Salt / sulfate deposit
evaporite.description: Evaporite lakes and salt flats. Terrain says little; mineral layers (CRISM) are needed.

slope.label: Slope distribution
slope.method: Wasserstein distance between slope histograms (scale 8 deg)
slope.description: How steep the ground is at every pixel. The whole spread of steepness is compared, not just the average.

roughness.label: Surface roughness
roughness.method: Wasserstein distance of log10 Terrain Ruggedness Index (scale 0.3)
roughness.description: How bumpy the ground is: the average height difference between each pixel and its 8 neighbours (Terrain Ruggedness Index).

hypsometry.label: Hypsometry
hypsometry.method: Mean gap between normalised elevation-area curves (scale 0.08)
hypsometry.description: How much of the area is high ground versus low ground, i.e. the shape of the landscape's elevation distribution.

profile.label: Crater profile shape
profile.method: Mean correlation of 8 compass-sector radial profiles with the target profile (r/R 0-1.5)
profile.description: Whether the site has the same bowl-and-rim shape in all 8 compass directions as the target crater. Distances are divided by the crater radius, so different-sized craters can be compared.

depth.label: Depth / diameter
depth.method: Log-ratio of depth/diameter (score 0.5 at a 2x difference)
depth.description: How deep the crater is relative to its width (rim height minus floor, divided by diameter).

flat_fraction.label: Flat ground (< 5 deg)
flat_fraction.method: Difference in the share of area flatter than 5 deg (scale 0.15)
flat_fraction.description: Share of the ground flatter than 5 degrees: where a lander or habitat could sit.

illumination.label: Sunlight at low sun
illumination.method: Wasserstein distance of per-pixel lit fraction over 16 sun azimuths at the target's sun elevation, with body curvature (scale 0.15)
illumination.description: From how many of 16 directions each spot gets sunlight when the Sun is just above the horizon (1.5 degrees at the lunar south pole). Computed from terrain shadows out to 20 km, including the planet's curvature.

texture.label: Terrain texture
texture.method: Mean gap between normalised log power spectra, 100 m - 20 km wavelengths (scale 0.3)
texture.description: The pattern of hills and hollows at scales from 100 m to 20 km (shape of the terrain's power spectrum).

thermal_amplitude.label: Day-night temperature swing
thermal_amplitude.description: How much the surface temperature changes between day and night. Earth: MODIS mean (day - night) at the ~10:30 / 22:30 overpasses, June-August. Moon: Diviner max - min over a full lunar day in southern summer. Mars: THEMIS afternoon minus pre-dawn, northern summer. The bodies differ by 10-100x, so sites are scored by the ratio of their typical (median) swing.

sources.earth: Google Earth Engine: MODIS/061/MOD11A2 (LST_Day_1km - LST_Night_1km, Jun-Aug)
sources.mars: Mars Odyssey THEMIS projected brightness temperature (ASU / NASA PDS): mean afternoon (12-17 h) minus mean pre-dawn (0-7 h), northern summer
sources.moon: LRO Diviner 240 m south-polar temperatures (Williams et al. 2019), via UCLA / PDS

thermal_amplitude.code: analog/layers.py: site_values(), compare_layer(); files in data/layers/thermal_amplitude/
thermal_amplitude.method: Ratio of the two sites' median values; score = 0.5^(log(ratio)/log(4)): 1.0 when equal, 0.5 at a 4x difference, 0.25 at 16x.

albedo.label: Surface albedo

sources.earth: Google Earth Engine: MODIS/061/MCD43A3 (white-sky shortwave albedo)
sources.moon: NASA PDS: LRO LOLA normal albedo

albedo.code: analog/layers.py: site_values(), compare_layer(); files in data/layers/albedo/

barren_ground.label: Barren ground (no vegetation)
barren_ground.description: Share of the site where even peak-summer NDVI stays below 0.2: bare rock, sand, ice or water. The Moon and Mars have no vegetation, so their share is 100% by definition.

sources.earth: Google Earth Engine: MODIS/061/MOD13A2 (max NDVI, Jun-Aug)

barren_ground.code: analog/layers.py: site_values(), compare_layer(); files in data/layers/barren_ground/
barren_ground.method: Share of the area below 0.2 at each site; score = exp(-|difference| / 0.25). Moon and Mars use the known value 100%.

surface_dust.label: Surface dust / fine soil
surface_dust.description: Share of the site covered by fine dust or fine soil. Earth: bare ground whose topsoil is mostly silt + clay (> 50%). Mars: TES Dust Cover Index below 0.94 (dust-covered surface, Ruff & Christensen 2002). The two are measured differently (soil texture vs thermal-infrared emissivity), so each body has its own threshold. Moon: no data yet.

sources.earth: Google Earth Engine: OpenLandMap topsoil sand content (fine = 100 - sand) on barren ground (MODIS MOD13A2 NDVI < 0.2)
sources.mars: TES Dust Cover Index (Ruff & Christensen 2002), numeric 16 pixels/degree map from ASU
sources.moon: No data yet (PDS team: Diviner rock abundance / regolith fines)

surface_dust.code: analog/layers.py: site_values(), compare_layer(); files in data/layers/surface_dust/
surface_dust.method: Share of the area past each body's threshold (earth: above 50; mars: below 0.94); score = exp(-|difference| / 0.25).

radar_cpr.label: Radar circular polarization ratio
radar_cpr.description: Surface roughness / ice indicator from compact- or hybrid-polarimetry radar.

sources.moon: NASA PDS: LRO Mini-RF CPR mosaics

radar_cpr.code: analog/layers.py: site_values(), compare_layer(); files in data/layers/radar_cpr/

demo_tpi.label: Topographic position (demo)
demo_tpi.description: Elevation relative to the surrounding 2 km mean. Generated from the DEMs by scripts/make_demo_layers.py only to test the layer pipeline; it is not independent data.
demo_tpi.code: analog/layers.py: site_values(), compare_layer(); files in data/layers/demo_tpi/

earth_limits: Mars gravity is 0.38 g: crater walls, slopes and ejecta behave differently.
Atmosphere is ~0.6% of Earth's pressure, mostly CO2: no liquid water today.
No magnetic field: surface radiation far above Earth levels.
Mean surface temperature about -60 C.

arcadia.name: Arcadia Planitia
arcadia.source: Mars HRSC-MOLA Blended DEM v2, 200 m (USGS Astrogeology)
arcadia.blurb: Smooth, low plains with shallow buried water ice (SHARAD radar, SWIM project pilot area): a proposed human landing region.
earth_limits: Mars gravity is 0.38 g and the air is ~0.6% of Earth's pressure: ice sublimates instead of melting.
Ice here is buried under dry regolith; Earth permafrost has an active layer that thaws every summer.
No magnetic field: surface radiation far above Earth levels.
200 m elevation data cannot see metre-scale polygons; HiRISE DEMs would be needed.

coord_source.source: SWIM project pilot study centre, 196 E 47.25 N (LPSC 2019 abstract)

shackleton.name: Shackleton Crater
shackleton.source: LRO NAC 4 m stereo DEM (USGS, 'Moon LRO South Pole DEM') resampled to 20 m, LOLA LDEM_80S_80M fills the edges
shackleton.blurb: Rim lies almost on the south pole; permanently shadowed floor near Artemis candidate regions.
earth_limits: Moon gravity is 0.165 g: much deeper, steeper fresh craters for the same size.
Hard vacuum and no weathering: craters stay sharp for billions of years.
Permanently shadowed floors reach ~40 K (-233 C), colder than anywhere on Earth.
No atmosphere or magnetic field to block radiation and micrometeorites.

coord_source.source: Assistant's general knowledge; crater centre confirmed in the DEM (within ~1 km)

malapert.source: LRO LOLA polar DEM LDEM_80S_80M (NASA PDS Geosciences)
malapert.blurb: ~5 km high massif facing Earth: long sunlight on its heights and direct line of sight for communications.
earth_limits: At the lunar pole the Sun never rises more than ~1.5 deg: Earth sites only see this low sun part of the year.
Moon gravity is 0.165 g and there is no atmosphere: no wind, no erosion, regolith stays loose.
Day/night temperature swings of ~250 K in sunlit areas.
No atmosphere or magnetic field to block radiation and micrometeorites.

data_sources._comment: Where every dataset in the project comes from and how we got it. Shown in the viewer's 'Data sources' window. When a team adds a dataset, add an entry here. `dem_for` marks the elevation source used for each body. `agency` groups datasets in the viewer's source filter; layer datasets are referenced from config/layers.json `source_ids`.

datasets.name: Copernicus DEM GLO-30
datasets.measures: Ground surface height (m), from TanDEM-X radar, 2011-2015
datasets.provider: European Space Agency / European Union (Copernicus); TanDEM-X data by DLR and Airbus
datasets.how: analog/sources.py fetch_earth() works out which 1x1 degree tiles cover each site, then reads only the needed part of each Cloud-Optimized GeoTIFF over HTTP (GDAL /vsicurl/) from the public bucket copernicus-dem-30m.s3.amazonaws.com. No account needed.
datasets.used_for: All Earth sites: terrain metrics and 3D terrain
datasets.credit: Produced using Copernicus WorldDEM-30 (c) DLR e.V. 2010-2014 and (c) Airbus Defence and Space GmbH 2014-2018, provided under COPERNICUS by the European Union and ESA; all rights reserved.

datasets.name: Mars HRSC-MOLA Blended DEM v2
datasets.measures: Mars surface height (m), blending ESA Mars Express HRSC stereo and NASA MGS MOLA laser altimetry
datasets.provider: USGS Astrogeology Science Center (data: ESA / DLR / FU Berlin, NASA)

links.label: File we read (11 GB, only a window is downloaded)

datasets.how: analog/sources.py fetch_mars() reads only the rows and columns around each site from the global GeoTIFF over HTTP (GDAL /vsicurl/ range requests), then reprojects them onto a local metre grid using the Mars radius (3396.19 km).
datasets.credit: Fergason, R.L., Hare, T.M., Laura, J. (2018). HRSC and MOLA Blended Digital Elevation Model at 200m v2. USGS Astrogeology.

datasets.name: LRO LOLA south-pole DEM (LDEM_80S_80M)
datasets.measures: Moon surface height relative to a 1737.4 km sphere, from LOLA laser altimetry, 2009-2017
datasets.resolution: 80 m, polar stereographic, south of 80 S
datasets.provider: NASA Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter, LOLA team (Goddard); archived at NASA PDS Geosciences Node
datasets.how: analog/sources.py fetch_moon() uses the PDS label (LDEM_80S_80M_FLOAT.LBL) to compute which rows of the 920 MB raw file cover each site, downloads only those bytes with an HTTP Range request (12-34 MB per site), and converts km to m.
datasets.used_for: Shackleton Crater, Malapert Massif, Mons Mouton Plateau
datasets.credit: NASA / GSFC / LRO LOLA team, NASA Planetary Data System.

datasets.name: Moon LRO South Pole DEM (LRO NAC stereo, 4 m)
datasets.measures: Moon surface height (m, relative to the 1737.4 km sphere) from Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter Narrow Angle Camera stereo images
datasets.resolution: 4 m, polar stereographic, ~65 x 68 km around the south pole (irregular coverage)
datasets.provider: USGS Astrogeology (Astropedia), from NASA LRO NAC images
datasets.how: analog/sources.py merge_nac() downloads the file once (stored row by row, so a partial read would fetch most of it anyway) to data/external/moon/, resamples it onto Shackleton's grid at 20 m, removes the median vertical offset to LOLA measured where both have data, and uses LOLA only where NAC has no coverage.
datasets.used_for: Shackleton Crater (high-resolution terrain and 3D view); Malapert and Mons Mouton are outside its coverage
datasets.credit: USGS Astrogeology Science Center; NASA / GSFC / Arizona State University LRO Camera team.

datasets.name: Blue Marble Next Generation (January 2004)
datasets.resolution: Downscaled to 2048 x 1024 for the globe
datasets.how: Downloaded once and resized with Pillow.
datasets.used_for: Earth globe image only (not used in scores)
datasets.credit: NASA Earth Observatory, Blue Marble Next Generation.

datasets.name: CGI Moon Kit - LROC colour mosaic
datasets.used_for: Moon globe image only (not used in scores)

datasets.name: MGS MOLA global DEM (463 m)
datasets.provider: NASA Mars Global Surveyor MOLA team, via USGS Astrogeology
datasets.how: Every 22nd row of the 2 GB file is read over HTTP, then coloured by height and hill-shaded by our script, so the Mars globe shows real elevation data.
datasets.used_for: Mars globe image only (not used in scores)
datasets.credit: NASA / MGS MOLA Science Team; USGS Astrogeology.

datasets.name: MODIS Land Surface Temperature (MOD11A2 v6.1)
datasets.how: scripts/gee_export.py: Earth Engine averages (LST_Day_1km - LST_Night_1km) x 0.02 over June-August of the chosen year, clips each Earth site's box (scripts/site_bounds.py) and downloads one GeoTIFF per site with getDownloadURL into data/layers/thermal_amplitude/.
datasets.measures: Land surface temperature, day and night, 8-day composites (K, scale factor 0.02)
datasets.provider: NASA LP DAAC (Terra MODIS), via Google Earth Engine
datasets.credit: Wan, Z., Hook, S., Hulley, G. MODIS/Terra Land Surface Temperature/Emissivity 8-Day L3 Global 1km SIN Grid V061. NASA EOSDIS LP DAAC.

datasets.name: MODIS BRDF/Albedo (MCD43A3 v6.1)
datasets.how: Planned: delivered by the data team as GeoTIFFs via Google Earth Engine: MODIS/061/MCD43A3. Not downloaded yet.

datasets.name: RADARSAT Constellation Mission compact-pol
datasets.how: Planned: delivered by the data team as GeoTIFFs via EODMS (Natural Resources Canada). Not downloaded yet.

datasets.name: Mars Odyssey THEMIS projected brightness temperature (IRPBT v2)
datasets.access: NASA PDS Orbital Data Explorer (oderest.rsl.wustl.edu) + static.mars.asu.edu
datasets.how: scripts/themis_temperature.py asks the NASA PDS Orbital Data Explorer REST API for every THEMIS PBT image over each Mars target. Mars Odyssey only images at ~4-7 h and ~16-19 h local time, so it keeps sunlit late-afternoon images (15:30-18:30) and early-morning images (4:00-7:30) from the same 90-degree stretch of the Mars year (the one with the most of both; northern summer for our sites), downloads them (cached in data/external/mars/themis/), averages each set on the site grid and stores late afternoon minus early morning in data/layers/thermal_amplitude/<site>.tif.
datasets.measures: Surface brightness temperature (K) from single THEMIS infrared images, late afternoon (~17-18 h) and early morning (~5-7 h)
datasets.provider: Arizona State University THEMIS team, NASA Mars Odyssey; archived at NASA PDS (ODY-M-THM-5-IRPBT-V2.0)
datasets.credit: Christensen, P.R. et al., THEMIS, NASA Mars Odyssey / Arizona State University; NASA Planetary Data System.
datasets.caveat: Mars Odyssey only images at ~5-7 h and ~17-18 h local time, so this 'swing' is late afternoon minus early morning (~20 K), well below Mars's true day-night range. Mars temperature scores are therefore too generous to Earth sites with moderate swings. Untick this dataset in the Data sources filter to leave it out.

datasets.name: MGS TES albedo
datasets.how: Planned: delivered by the data team as GeoTIFFs via NASA PDS. Not downloaded yet.

datasets.name: LRO Diviner south-polar temperatures (240 m, PCP)
datasets.how: scripts/diviner_temperature.py binary-searches each ~200 MB summer table (rows are sorted by x) with HTTP Range requests and downloads only the strips around our Moon sites (~40 MB per table). It samples 12 sun positions across the lunar day and keeps max(T) - min(T) per 240 m pixel, saved as data/layers/thermal_amplitude/<moon site>.tif.
datasets.measures: Bolometric surface temperature (K), binned by sun position over 2009-2019
datasets.resolution: 240 m, polar stereographic, south of 80 S
datasets.provider: NASA LRO Diviner team, UCLA (Williams et al. 2019, JGR 124, 2505-2521); dataset LRO-L-DLRE-5-GCP-V1.0
datasets.credit: Williams, J.-P. et al. (2019), Seasonal polar temperatures on the Moon, JGR Planets 124, 2505-2521. NASA LRO Diviner team.

datasets.name: LRO Mini-RF CPR mosaics
datasets.how: Planned: delivered by the data team as GeoTIFFs via NASA PDS. Not downloaded yet.

datasets.name: MODIS Vegetation Indices (MOD13A2 v6.1)
datasets.provider: NASA LP DAAC (Terra MODIS), via Google Earth Engine
datasets.how: scripts/gee_export.py: Earth Engine takes the maximum NDVI over June-August (peak greenness) of the chosen year, clips each Earth site's box and downloads one GeoTIFF per site into data/layers/barren_ground/.
datasets.credit: Didan, K. MODIS/Terra Vegetation Indices 16-Day L3 Global 1km SIN Grid V061. NASA EOSDIS LP DAAC.

datasets.name: OpenLandMap topsoil sand content (v02)
datasets.measures: Sand content of the fine earth (%) at the surface (0 cm); fine fraction = 100 - sand
datasets.provider: OpenGeoHub / EnvirometriX (Hengl 2018), via Google Earth Engine. A machine-learning soil map predicted from soil profiles and satellite data, not a direct measurement.
datasets.how: scripts/gee_export.py: fine fraction = 100 - sand (band b0) where peak-summer NDVI (MOD13A2) is below 0.2, else 0, clipped to each Earth site's box and downloaded as one GeoTIFF per site into data/layers/surface_dust/.
datasets.credit: Hengl, T. (2018). Sand content in % (kg / kg) at 6 standard depths at 250 m resolution (v0.2). Zenodo. OpenLandMap.

datasets.name: TES Dust Cover Index (Ruff & Christensen 2002)
datasets.measures: Average thermal-infrared emissivity at 1350-1400 cm-1; fine dust lowers it (below ~0.94 = dust-covered)
datasets.provider: S. W. Ruff, Arizona State University, from NASA Mars Global Surveyor TES data
datasets.how: scripts/mars_dust.py downloads the numeric map (66 MB, float32, simple cylindrical -180..180, checked against known dusty and dust-free regions), cuts the area around each Mars target and saves data/layers/surface_dust/<site>.tif.
datasets.credit: Ruff, S.W. and Christensen, P.R. (2002), JGR 107(E12), 5127, doi:10.1029/2001JE001580.
